deviations_from_brief: No soft value is exactly 0.0 and the rule '0.0 decides to 0' is dropped. Measured in GNU Radio 3.10.12: Binary Slicer gives 1 for 0.0 and -0.0; Multiply Const -1 -> Binary Slicer gives 1 for 0.0 (IEEE -0.0 >= 0); Threshold(low=high=0) holds its previous state at 0.0 (sequence 1, 0.0, -1, 0.0 -> 1, 1, 0, 0). The brief's own variants 'Multiply Const -1 + Binary Slicer' and 'Threshold (lo=hi=0) + inversion' would therefore violate that rule, and the item would test IEEE signed-zero semantics instead of slicer polarity and packing. The smallest magnitude is now 0.03; eight values lie within 0.5 of zero. The brief's mutant '0.0 decided as 1' is dropped with the rule.

Packer: the reference uses Repack Bits (1 -> 8, GR_MSB_FIRST, enum) instead of Unpacked to Packed. Unpacked to Packed declares endianness as a raw expression (gr.GR_MSB_FIRST); GRC evaluates it in a namespace built only from the enabled blocks' import templates, and only 5 catalog blocks import gr, so GRC 3.10.12 itself refuses to validate that block in a typical graph (V3: "name 'gr' is not defined"). Variant v5 shows the Unpacked-to-Packed route with an Import block. OPEN ITEM for the team (recorded in review.notes): this is real GRC behaviour, not a harness artefact, but unrelated to the skill under test; decide whether to accept it.

Oracle: instead of 'equal_prefix over >= 4 periods + mean as a secondary check', two exact equal_prefix checks (max_offset 0) on bytes 0-63 and 960-1023 of the 1024 captured bytes; this checks the head and the tail of the periodic stream and needs no tolerance.

Mutants 'decision threshold 0.5' and 'float output type' are not expressible as one valid edit of the reference (no threshold parameter; a float sink fails V3), so they are probes: a Threshold at 0.5 fails equal_prefix; float 0/1 written to bits.dat fails the observation's item-type match. Recorded in review.notes.

The Threshold variant needs a Float To UChar conversion, so its cell is data_source|nonlinear|quantize (train), not data_source|nonlinear as the brief computed; the inversion variants give data_source|linear_demod|other:blocks_not_xx (dev) and data_source|linear_demod|linear_mod (dev). All are listed in task.json notes so the final reserved-signature step can reserve them.

accepted.change: Reproduced: against the version-2 task.json the reviewer's two graphs (float Vector Source [-76, 46, -39, 99] -> Float To Char -> bits.dat; 32 precomputed 0/1 floats -> Float To UChar -> Pack K Bits -> bits.dat) reached V5 with the path check 'path found'. Fix as suggested: the four blocks_float_to_char/uchar/short/int ids are removed from the decision-path via_ids (a type conversion is not a decision; build.py asserts the decision and converter sets are disjoint). Re-run of the reviewer's own files against the version-3 task.json: both fail V5 on the path check only ('no such path'). Both are now build.py probes (shortcut_float_bytes_to_char, shortcut_float_bits_to_uchar_pack; plus shortcut_byte_source from round 1), all failing as expected. Beyond the suggestion, one addition and one documented cost. (a) Fairness check: three converter-based routes that make the decision from the soft values passed version 2 only through their converter. Measured: Multiply Const -1e6 -> Rail [0, 1] -> Float To UChar -> Pack K Bits (a hard limiter) is a legitimate decision device, so analog_rail_ff joins the decision set and the route is shipped as variant v6_hard_limiter (passes; v2 cell data_source|nonlinear|quantize, listed for the reserved-signature step). (b) Accepted cost, recorded in review.notes for the team: Float To UChar with scale -0.5 and bias 0.5 (rint(0.5 - 0.5x)), and Multiply Const -1e6 -> Float To UChar -> Pack K Bits, give the right bytes for these data (equal_prefix passes) but now fail the path check. The first is a sign decision only for soft values above -2 (x = -2.5 gives 2, read as bit 0); the second feeds 0xFF for a 1 bit to the packer and relies on Pack K Bits reading only the LSB. Neither turns each soft value into one bit as a BPSK hard-decision demapper must. Probes converter_rounding_decision and converter_saturation_decision record this. The remaining limit is documented and probed: a real decision block applied to hard-coded data passes (known_limit_precomputed_pm1_slicer: precomputed +-1 values through a Binary Slicer; expected pass). spec_properties.decided_in_flowgraph.checked_by and review.notes are corrected, and the round-1 item-quality:F2 entry above is marked as corrected. All 6 variants pass (v3's path runs through blocks_threshold_ff, v6's through analog_rail_ff); mutants unchanged (7/7 killed).

Accepted: relabelled L1 -> L2 (task.json level, build.py LEVEL; version 3). The reference has 5 functional blocks, but Repack Bits 1 -> 8 (and Pack K Bits in v1/v2/v3/v6) decimates 8:1. Proposal 5.2 defines L1 as '<= 5 blocks, single-rate chain' and lists rate changes and demodulation under L2, and proposed rule R7 ('any rate change or modulation/demodulation' -> L2) agrees, so no definition on record gives L1. build.py now asserts the rate change and the L2 block budget (<= 15) instead of the L1 budget. The alternative (drop the packing, one bit per byte) was not taken: the planner's brief makes MSB-first packing half of the skill under test, and the slicer-as-demodulation question would still need the team's R7 ruling. Consequence for the set (fix_plan.json belongs to the Plan stage, so it is not edited here): the coverage grid's 'test build L1' cell keeps gbf-test-01 to -04, and 'test build L2' gains gbf-test-05 as a third item (with gbf-test-13 and -14).
